_note: Gun drilling starting values. Tables are transcribed from the makers' PDFs, each read twice on 2026-11-12. Nothing is averaged; where makers differ both are shown.

STERLING.title: Gun drill catalogue, 'Speeds and Feeds' (speed chart, approximate feed rate, oil pressure and GPM)
STERLING.note: Maker. Speed chart by material and hardness for high pressure and for spray mist; feed per revolution by diameter in six material columns; oil pressure, flow and maximum unsupported length by diameter; RPM = SFM / 0.262 / diameter; over 30:1 reduce the feed by 20 %. The column headings of the feed table are broken up in the PDF text: see docs/sources.md for how they were read.

BOTEK.title: Catalogue ELB/ZLB (single-flute and two-flute gundrills), guide values for Type 110, pp. 20-21
BOTEK.note: Maker. Cutting speed ranges for four steel groups and feed ranges by drill diameter (p. 20). The coolant pressure and quantity recommendations are charts and could not be read. Page 21 (other materials) has no diameter column in the text and is not used.

UNISIG.title: Deep hole drilling technical reference
UNISIG.note: Machine builder. Approximate starting coolant flow for deep hole drilling in general: 3.7 to 4.5 l/min per mm of tool diameter (25 to 30 gal/min per inch); 'parameter values change by tooling type'. Speed and feed are left to the tool maker.

MASTERFLUID.title: Technical bulletin 109, Gun drilling (2014, revised 2020)
MASTERFLUID.note: Coolant maker. Water-based coolant: supply enough per drill revolution to fill the drilled hole; volume in gallons = 0.785 x diameter^2 x depth / 231, flow = volume x rpm (3/8 in x 8 in at 300 rpm is about 1.1 GPM). Oils run at a lower flow. The single coolant hole is about one quarter of the drill diameter. Checked and not shown on the page: see 'Read and not used'.

CTE2016.title: Conventional thinking (gundrilling on conventional machines), 1 Jan 2016
CTE2016.note: Trade magazine quoting makers. Drill Masters Eldorado: 200 to 400 psi may do on drills 2 in and larger, 1,500 psi and higher for tiny holes; 10 to 12 % emulsion. UNISIG: 1,000 psi (69 bar) is common on Swiss-type lathes, most gundrilling machines give two to three times that. Sterling: a 0.250 in gundrill in steel might feed at 0.0005 ipr; pilot hole 1 to 2 diameters deep and 0.0005 to 0.0010 in larger than the gundrill. Star SU: straightness typically 0.001 in per inch of depth. Iscar: keep the fluid at 70 to 75 F, not above 130 F.

HARTNER.title: Catalogue pages 474-475, single-fluted deep hole drills
HARTNER.note: Maker. Pilot hole 1.5 x D deep, tolerance H8; enter the pilot hole at about 200 rev/min and 500 mm/min; soluble oil with at least 10 % oil. Its speed table could not be matched to materials in the PDF text and is not used.

INGERSOLL.title: Catalogue excerpts, gun drills
INGERSOLL.note: Maker. Pilot hole length 1.5 x D; water-soluble concentration under 8 % not acceptable, 10 to 12 % acceptable, 12 to 15 % preferred. Its speed table is by material number without the names in the text and is not used.

ISCAR.title: Machining conditions for indexable gundrills (e-catalogue information sheet 4448)
ISCAR.note: Maker. Filter the coolant to under 20 um; keep it at 20 to 22 C (above 50 C it stops working); 10 to 15 % concentration. Its speeds and feeds are for indexable drills of 10 to 26 mm, a different tool, and its pressure chart is a picture: neither is used.

botek._label_note: In the PDF text the diameter labels of the rows under 10 mm carry a stray '1' ('11.85 - 12.49', '6.00 - 16.99'). They are read as 1.85-2.49 ... 9.00-9.99: the upper limits then run 2.49, 2.99 ... 9.99 without a gap up to the clean row 10.00-11.99, and Type 110 starts at 1.85 mm.

rules.t: Start in a guide bushing or a pilot hole. Pilot hole: 1 to 2 diameters deep and 0.0005 to 0.0010 in (0.013 to 0.025 mm) larger than the gundrill (Sterling, quoted in Cutting Tool Engineering); 1.5 x D deep (Hartner, to H8; Ingersoll).
Do not run a gundrill at speed outside the hole: it whips. Sterling's table gives the longest unsupported length by diameter; Hartner says to enter the pilot hole at about 200 rev/min and 500 mm/min.

Flow matters more than pressure: the chips leave only if enough coolant reaches the tip. Pressure rises as the drill gets smaller: 200 to 400 psi can be enough on 2 in drills, 1,500 psi and more on very small ones (Drill Masters Eldorado); about 1,000 psi (69 bar) is common on Swiss-type lathes and most gundrilling machines give two to three times that (UNISIG).

Water-soluble coolant: 10 to 12 % (Drill Masters Eldorado; Ingersoll calls 10 to 12 % acceptable and 12 to 15 % preferred, under 8 % not acceptable), 10 to 15 % (ISCAR), at least 10 % oil (Hartner). botek rates deep-hole drilling oil as highly suitable and emulsion as suitable to a limited degree.
Keep the coolant clean and cool: filtered to under 20 um and at 20 to 22 C (ISCAR); 70 to 75 F and not above 130 F (ISCAR, quoted in Cutting Tool Engineering).
Over 30 diameters deep, reduce the feed by 20 % (Sterling). The page does this when a depth is entered.
Straightness to expect: typically 0.001 in per inch of depth (Star SU, quoted in Cutting Tool Engineering).

not_used.title: Fill-the-hole flow rule and nozzle formula (technical bulletin 109)
not_used.why: Both examples are reproduced by the core tests, but the rule is not shown: at gundrill speeds it asks for several times the makers' flow (32 gal/min for a 1/2 in drill 16.5 in deep at 2,284 rpm, where Sterling gives 7), more than a coolant hole of a quarter of the diameter passes by the bulletin's own nozzle formula (about 10.7 gal/min at 525 psi).
